Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, L.A.C. No. 58/2019 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'RFCTLA Act' for short) for apportionment of compensation amount.

sentences.text: .2. The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing Sy.No.39 measuring 2 acres of Donenahalli village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bangaluru South Taluka has been acquired for the purpose of construction of houses.
Preliminary notification was issued on 19.03.2011.
Final notification was published in the Gazette on 27.11.2012.
The award was passed on 02.09.2015.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs.2,16,42,800/-.
As there was a dispute regarding title of the documents, the L.A.O. has sent the reference to this Court and has deposited a sum of Rs. 2,16,42,800/-.

The said amount has been kept in F.D. in the Bank of Baroda, Bannerghatta Branch, Bengaluru - 83.
.3.
After receipt of reference, this court issued notices to the claimants.
The claimants 1 to 4 have appeared through their counsels.
The claimant No.5 L.A.C. No.58/2019 and 6 remained absent.
The claimants 1 to 4 filed separate claim statements.

.4. Claimant No.1(a) to (c) and claimant No. 3(a) and (b) filed claim statement claiming that the property in Survey No. 39 measuring 2 acres of Donenahalli village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bangaluru South Taluka granted in favour of claimant No.1 Narasimhaiah under grant proceeding bearing No.
LND/RUC/CR/1296/91- 92.
The original grantee Narasimhaiah / claimant No.1 died on 06.03.2011.
After the death of claimant No.1 Narasimhaiah, the property was changed to the name of claimant No.2 under MR No.T5/2016-17.
It is further stated that the above property has been acquired by the respondent under Preliminary Notification dated 19.03.2011 and Final Notification dated 27.11.2012.
It is further stated that the Claimant No.1(a) to (c) and claimant No. 3(a) and (b) are the children and grand children of claimant No.1 Narasimhaiah.
As such, after the death of Narasimhaiah, they have succeeded to the L.A.C. No. 58/2019 property.

Accordingly they are entitled for compensation along with claimant No.2.
.5.

Claimant No.2 Smt. Chikkatayamma filed a claim statement wherein she claims that she is the daughter in law of original grantee Narasimhaiah and the property granted to Narasimhaiah under LND RUC CR 1296/91-92.
The said Narasimhaiah died on 06.03.2011.

In order to prove their cases, the claimant No.1(a) and grand son of claimant No.1 namely N.

The documents got marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.
The claimant No.4 though filed claim statement not chosen to lead any evidence.

.8. On the basis of the above, the points for consideration are that:
1) Whether the Claimant No.1(a) to (c), claimant No.2 and claimant No. 3(a) and (b)
are the absolute owners of the acquired property and entitled for the compensation amount in respect of Survey No.39 measuring 2 acres of Donenahalli village,

Further it is an admitted and undisputed fact that the award was passed on 02.09.2015 and the L.A.O. has fixed the compensation L.A.C. No.58/2019 of Rs.2,16,42,800/- and the said amount has been kept in F.D. in the Bank of Baroda,

sentences.text:
As per the records, the claimant No.1 is one Narasimhaiah, claimant No.2 is Smt.
Chikkatayamma, claimant No.3 is Smt. Venkatalakshmamma and claimant No.4 is Smt. Siddamma along with Tahsildar and Assistant Director of Land Records of Bengaluru.
During pendency of the case, the claimants 1 and 3 were died and their LRs are brought on record.
The claimant No.1 and 3 together claim right over the acquired property.
Similarly, the claimant No.4 claiming right over the acquired property.
However, the claimants 5 and 6 not at all claiming any right over the acquired property and hence, rival claim in this case is between claimants 1 to 3 and claimant No.4.

As such,
the Court has to consider that who is having right, title and interest over the acquired property, so that the Court can decide the apportionment of compensation.
As stated above, the claimant No.1 Narasimhaiah died during pendency of the case and his LRs are brought on record as claimant No. 1(a) to (c).

Similarly the claimant No. 3 died during pendency of the case and her LRs are brought on record as claimant No.3(a) and (b).
.13.

The claimant No.1(a) to (c) and claimant No. 3(a) and (b) are permitted to come on record as surviving LRs of claimant No.1 on the basis of the Genealogical tree produced in support of their application that had been marked in the case as Ex.P.19.
Ex .P.19 is the family Genealogical tree issued by the Tahsildar, Bangaluru South Taluka who is competent authority to issued the same.
As per the said family Genealogical tree, the claimant No.1 Narasimhaiah is the son of late. Adina Kadaraiah.
Said Narasimhaiah had the first wife by name Bylamma who died on 10.06.1977 and Venkatalaxmamma was his second wife died on 27.04.2018.

As per Ex.P.19, claimant No.1 Narasimhaiah had a son by name Narasimhamurthy L.A.C. No.58/2019 and the said son Narasimhamurthy died as on 11.11.2009 leaving behind his wife Chikkatayamma and 3 children namely Srinivasa K.N. Devaraju and Sathyanarayana.
The said Chikka Tayamma is already arrayed as claimant No.2 in this case.
After the death of Narasimhaiah, his grand children namely Srinivasa K.N., Devaraju and Sathyanarayana were impleaded as claimant No. 1(a) to (c).
As per Genealogical tree, the claimant No.3 Smt. Venkatalakshmamma is second wife of late.

Narasimhaiah and the said Venkatalakshmamma died as on 27.04.2018 leaving behind her two daughters namely Smt.
Anjinamma and Smt. Anupama as claimant No. 3(a) and (b) in this case.
Therefore, considering the family Genealogical tree, LRs of claimants 1 and 3 were impleaded as claimant No. 1(a) to (c) and claimant No.3(a) and (b).

It is relevant to note that father of claimant No.3(a) and (b) are the children born to Narasimhaiah/claimant No.1 through his second wife Venkatalaxmamma, as such,
the claimant No. 1(a) to (c), claimant No.2 and claimant L.A.C. No. 58/2019 No.3(a) and (b) are together succeeded to the estate left by claimant No.1 Narasimhaiah.
.14.
Now it is to be considered that who has shown right, title and interest over the acquired property in view of the rival claims over the acquired property between claimants 1 to 3 and claimant No.4.
Though the claimant No.4 filed a claim statement not chosen to lead any evidence nor produced any documentary evidence in support of her claim.

.15. As stated earlier, the claimants 1 to 3 got examined claimant No. 1(a) N. Srinivas as PW.1 by filing evidence affidavit, wherein, he stated in-consonance with the claim statement and also produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19 including RTC extract.
It is relevant to note that 2 acres of land in Survey No. 39 has been acquired by LAO in this case.

Ex.P.1 is the Form No.50 Narasimhaiah vs Slao Karnataka Housing Board on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127153437/
5 which is an application filed by the claimant No.1 for regularization of his unauthorized occupation over the property bearing Survey No. 39.

entities.text: Form No.50 Narasimhaiah vs Slao Karnataka Housing
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the grant order under Ex.P.3, 3 acres 10 guntas of land in L.A.C. No.58/2019 Survey No. 39 had been granted to claimant No.1.
However, Ex.P.5 sketch and Ex.P.6 Index of land disclose about the encroachment and possession of the property in Survey No.39 by the claimant No.1.
The Serial No.8 at Ex.P.6 discloses that Narasimhaiah was in possession of 2 acres of land.
Ex . P.8
discloses that one Motaiah is in possession of 2 acres 20 guntas and Narasimhaiah S/o late.
Adina Kadaraiah is in possession of 3 acres 10 guntas of land.
The entries also shows that claimants 1 to 3 are in possession of 2 acres of land in Survey No.39.
Therefore, the material placed before the Court sufficiently shows that the claimants 1 to 3 are in actual possession and enjoyment of acquired property.

Infact, there is no material on record to disbelieve the said claim of claimants 1 to 3.
.16.
In the case on hand, PW.1 has been thoroughly cross-examined by claimant No.4 but nothing has been elicited to show that these claimants have no right over the acquired property.
The claimant No.4 tried to make out a case that the property of the L.A.C. No. 58/2019 claimants 1 to 3 measuring 2 acres of land not identified.
The said fact cannot be accepted in view of various sketches produced by claimants.
Apart from that it is not the case of claimant No.1 and claimant No.4 that both are claiming right over the same property.
Further the claimant No.4 also not made out any case to show that her property has been identified.

Further if at all property in Survey No. 39 had been granted to her husband Motaiah for upset price, certainly she would have produced some documentary proof to substantiate the said fact but she fails to produce either oral or documentary evidence so that the Court can accept her claim.
As stated earlier, absolutely there is no material whatsoever on record to show that the claimant No.4 had any right over the acquired property.
.17. Therefore, claimant No. 1(a) to (c), claimant No. 2 and claimant No.3(a) and (b) are entitled for compensation amount involved in this case.
The claimant No.4 fails to make out any case to show that L.A.C. No.58/2019 she has any right over the acquired property and hence, her claim statement cannot be accepted.

Therefore, in the case on hand, this Court is of the humble opinion that the claimants 1 to 3 have made out sufficient grounds to accept their case that they are entitled for compensation amount in respect of acquired property.
Accordingly, the above point No. 1 is answered in the affirmative and point No.2 is answered in the negative.
.18. Point No.3:

In view of my findings on the above points 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The reference made by the respondent/SLAO under Section 77(1) of the Right to Fair compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 in respect of claimant No.1(a) to (c), claimant No.2 and claimant No.3(a) and (b) is hereby allowed.
